# Enterprise Architecture Practice (EAP) — FY27 Goal Roadmap

**Owner:** Mike Goppert | **Fiscal Year:** FY2027 (Apr 2026 – Mar 2027)

---
page_texts.2:
[strategy/goals/fy27/goals.md#executive-summary]

## Executive Summary

This roadmap aligns the Enterprise Architecture Practice to the CTO's FY27 strategic objectives. Each EA OKR maps directly to a CTO goal, and the roadmap initiatives represent the execution plan to deliver against those objectives. Initiatives are prioritized P0 (critical path), P1 (committed), P2 (planned), and P3 (stretch).

---
page_texts.3:
[strategy/goals/fy27/goals.md#cto-goal-alignment]

## CTO Goal Alignment

| CTO Goal ID | CTO Goal | EA Focus Area |
|-------------|----------|---------------|
| CTO-O1 | DDI Delivery — Deliver all DDI at cost and on-time | DDI engagement framework, governance checkpoints, standardized templates |
| CTO-O3 | Operational Excellence — Proactive vs Reactive | HA/DR reference architectures, observability standards, operational readiness gates |
| CTO-O5 | Enterprise Architecture — Drive EA governance across all programs | Domain models, CoP, reference architectures, TOPS review gates, EAP engagement model |
| CTO-O6 | Security Engineering — Embed security into engineering pipelines | Zero-trust Golden Path, security gates in CI/CD, consolidated code scanning |
| CTO-O7 | AI Adoption — Drive AI use cases to production | AI engineering foundation, AI Gateway, agentic AI coding framework |
| CTO-O8 | Training & Career Development | Certifications, Town Halls, CoP skill development |

---
page_texts.5:
[strategy/goals/fy27/goals.md#okr-1-ddi-delivery-15-weight--cto-o1]

### OKR 1: DDI Delivery (15% weight) — CTO-O1

**Objective:** Deliver all DDI at cost and on-time with embedded EA governance

**Key Results:**

- Formal DDI engagement framework established with defined roles, responsibilities, and governance checkpoints
- Standardized DDI templates and meeting cadence adopted across all DDI delivery teams
- EA participation in all major DDI initiatives with architecture review gates in place
- DDI governance framework implemented aligned to Gainwell EAP governance framework

**Owners:** Jim Yang, Jonathan Pepper, Michael Walter

---
page_texts.6:
[strategy/goals/fy27/goals.md#okr-2-operational-excellence-15-weight--cto-o3]

### OKR 2: Operational Excellence (15% weight) — CTO-O3

**Objective:** Ensure High Availability and Reliability of Hybrid Cloud Services

**Key Results:**

- Reference architectures published supporting HA/DR patterns (microservices, event-driven, CQRS, data lake)
- Observability standards and best practices defined for application instrumentation
- Operational excellence patterns and guidance documented and published to engineering teams
- Technology portfolio assessment completed to identify platform sprawl and consolidation opportunities
- Architecture review gates established for operational readiness (runbook, monitoring, alerting requirements)

**Owners:** Mike Goppert, James Macurak, Josh Oh, Jesse Adams

---
page_texts.7:
[strategy/goals/fy27/goals.md#okr-3-enterprise-architecture-practice-25-weight--cto-o5]

### OKR 3: Enterprise Architecture Practice (25% weight) — CTO-O5

**Objective:** Drive enterprise architecture practice at Gainwell enterprise

**Key Results:**

- Domain models published for all 4+ major product lines (C&E, Fiscal, PBM, Provider, Member) with bounded contexts defined
- Communities of Practice (CoP) established with regular cadence and measurable participation
- Reference architectures published for microservices, event-driven, CQRS, data lake, and API-first patterns
- EA contribution traceable to 2+ program wins or renewals
- TOPS and post-product review gates implemented for all major delivery efforts
- EAP engagement model fully operational in GainwellNow
- Technology portfolio rationalized using convergence framework

**Owners:** Mike Goppert, Core EA Team

---
page_texts.8:
[strategy/goals/fy27/goals.md#okr-4-security-engineering-15-weight--cto-o6]

### OKR 4: Security Engineering (15% weight) — CTO-O6

**Objective:** Embed security into all engineering pipelines and product delivery

**Key Results:**

- Zero-trust controls embedded in Golden Path templates aligned with HITRUST requirements
- Security gates enforced at all critical pipeline stages (build, test, deploy)
- Pattern for CI/CD pipelines integrated with security tooling (SAST, SCA, secrets scanning)
- Single consolidated code scanning platform adopted across all product lines
- Threat modeling tool integrated into pipeline for production deployments

**Owners:** Jesse Adams, Shashank Kharel, Mike Goppert, James Macurak

---
page_texts.9:
[strategy/goals/fy27/goals.md#okr-5-ai-adoption-20-weight--cto-o7]

### OKR 5: AI Adoption (20% weight) — CTO-O7

**Objective:** Drive AI use cases to production

**Key Results:**

- AI engineering foundation established for Provider+, Provider Everywhere, and Member Eligibility with business capabilities mapped
- AI Gateway as production platform offering for all agentic AI development
- Agentic AI coding framework and agent skill suite solidified, reducing time-to-market and cost on 3+ product development efforts

**Owners:** Mike Goppert, Josh Oh, James Macurak, Soma Natarajan, Subbu Muthu, Karthik Jeeva

---
page_texts.10:
[strategy/goals/fy27/goals.md#okr-6-training--career-development-10-weight--cto-o8]

### OKR 6: Training & Career Development (10% weight) — CTO-O8

**Objective:** Drive career advancement through certifications and community engagement

**Key Results:**

- Quarterly Town Halls delivered for training, development, and org updates
- AWS and Azure cloud certifications achieved across EA team (Target: 5+ certifications)
- Engineering community engagement through CoP with documented skill development outcomes

**Owners:** Mike Goppert, EAP Core Team

page_texts.22:
[strategy/goals/fy27/goals.md#risk-summary]

## Risk Summary

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|-----------|
| EA-R015 (EAP Engagement Model) is Off Track | Blocks demand intake and business alignment visibility | Escalate citizen developer effort; assess scope reduction |
| EA-R011/R012 data initiatives depend on domain decomposition | Data standards delayed if bounded contexts not defined early | Parallel-path data domain identification where possible |
| HITRUST certification timeline (EA-R006) spans full year | Compliance gap if delayed | Incremental e1 first, i1 follows |
| MDM initiative requires data governance and SME capacity | Platform may be ready before business rules are defined | Early stakeholder engagement for domain ownership |
| Multiple "Not Started" initiatives targeting Jun 2026 start | Q2 ramp-up bottleneck | Prioritize staffing and resource allocation in Q1 |
